pageProps.title: The Locked Room Murder Game
pageProps.review: A review of Shogo Utano's novel The Locked Room Murder Game, where an actual murder is given as a problem in a mystery game, introducing honest impressions of its disappointing forced development and unnatural behavior of characters despite the ingenious setup.
pageProps.description: I didn't kill because there was someone I wanted to kill, I killed because there was a trick I wanted to try.
pageProps.content:
## Review Five anonymous people gather on the internet to play a murder mystery game. Each person takes a turn as the culprit and presents a murder case as a problem, while the others solve it. But the murder case problem is not a fictional problem, but an actual murder case committed by the person playing the role of the culprit.
This concept is interesting, but there were some forced parts that reduced immersion. The situation of not getting caught despite the tricks not being that great, and characters who are good at devising tricks for their own murders but become stupid when inferring others' cases.
Perhaps because I watched it with too much expectation, the disappointment was quite large.
